title: Problems with many CRAN mirrors
description:
Thanks for the super package.

I'm noticing a problem when using certain CRAN mirrors. I've tracked this down to three root causes:

1. If a CRAN mirror does not use the web root of their URL, foghorn fails.  For example, the main CRAN mirror I use is `https://www.stats.bris.ac.uk/R/` where I've identified that the `/R` path is the problem.
2. Not all CRAN mirrors seem to support the canonical `/package=<pkg>` URL schema. For example, [https://www.stats.bris.ac.uk/R/package=mlmc](https://www.stats.bris.ac.uk/R/package=mlmc) works, but [https://cran.asia/package=mlmc](https://cran.asia/package=mlmc) does not do the correct redirect.
3. foghorn seems to automatically attempt to promote all CRAN mirrors to https. Some mirrors are http, but will support promoting the connection to https, whilst others are http only (eg [http://mirror.fcaglp.unlp.edu.ar/CRAN](http://mirror.fcaglp.unlp.edu.ar/CRAN))

To see these issues in action, when I run the code:

```r
for(i in 1:nrow(getCRANmirrors())) {
  chooseCRANmirror(ind = i)
  tryCatch({
    cran_details("mlmc")
    cran_results("louis.aslett@durham.ac.uk")
    n_cran_flavors()
    cli::cli_alert_success(paste0("Success for mirror ", i, " => ", getOption("repos")[[1]]))
  },
  error = \(e) cli::cli_alert_warning(paste0("Failed for mirror ", i, " => ", getOption("repos")[[1]])))
}
```

Therefore, at the moment foghorn only fully works with about 19% of CRAN mirrors.

I have forked foghorn and prepared a fix to the first 2 of these problems.  I will link the PR to this issue in a few minutes. description:
`foghorn` had been very reliable for me in automating analysis of reverse dependencies.  For 'recently' (weeks or months ago) it stopped and no longer retrieved results.  Without having looked at the code, I may be missing a package you use for scraping so maybe you skip the step silently?

Compare my existing (default) call with no extras:

```r
> cran_results(pkg=c("leidenAlg", "statgenGWAS"))
# A tibble: 0 × 7
# ℹ 7 variables: package <chr>, error <int>, fail <int>, warn <int>, note <int>, ok <int>, has_other_issues <lgl>
> 
```

which used to work.  "Lucky for me" there is an alternative:

````r
> cran_results(pkg=c("leidenAlg", "statgenGWAS"), src="crandb")
# A tibble: 2 × 7
  package     error  fail  warn  note    ok has_other_issues
  <chr>       <int> <int> <int> <int> <int> <lgl>           
1 leidenAlg       7     0     0     4     0 FALSE           
2 statgenGWAS     0     0     0    13     0 FALSE           
> 
```

If I misunderstood or missed something let me know.  The above seems to align with the basic package documentation, used to work, and should maybe warn in the former.   Thanks for putting this helpful package together.

title: [CRAN] documentation issue
description:
```
You have file 'foghorn/man/foghorn.Rd' with \docType{package}, likely
intended as a package overview help file, but without the appropriate
PKGNAME-package \alias as per "Documenting packages" in R-exts.

This seems to be the consequence of the breaking change

  Using @docType package no longer automatically adds a -package alias.
  Instead document _PACKAGE to get all the defaults for package
  documentation.

in roxygen2 7.0.0 (2019-11-12) having gone unnoticed, see
<https://github.com/r-lib/roxygen2/issues/1491>.

As explained in the issue, to get the desired PKGNAME-package \alias
back, you should either change to the new approach and document the new
special sentinel

  "_PACKAGE"

or manually add

  @aliases foghorn-package

if remaining with the old approach.

Please fix in your master sources as appropriate, and submit a fixed
version of your package within the next few months.
```

title: check on definitions of categories
description:
There is some discussion of CRAN categories [here](https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-package-devel/2020q4/006151.html);  it would be a good idea to take a look at the `cran_incoming` documentation and see if it's still accurate ...

```
this is a bit tricky since the documentation on the dashboard comes from an official, authoritative, source: the R journal [1].

"pending: if a decision is pending a response from the package maintainer: If an additional issue was present in the package that we cannot check for in the incoming checks (such as the BLAS issues mentioned in the section above), the maintainer is automatically asked whether these issues have been fixed. Same is true for change of maintainer (or maintainer's mail address) where the old maintainer (old address) is automatically asked to confirm the maintainer change. The answers have to be processed manually."

As Dirk explains and as reported in https://github.com/lockedata/cransays/issues/29, it is likely not true anymore but in the absence of further official information, it is difficult to issue a fix.

A later issue of the R journal [2] introduces the "waiting" and "newbies" categories but does not expand on the new role of "pending".

Best,

Hugo

[1]: https://journal.r-project.org/archive/2018-1/cran.pdf
[2]: https://journal.r-project.org/archive/2019-1/cran.pdf
```

title: Report modification date in cran_details()?
description:
It seems that we can query the modification date for check result files. Right now, winch sees a warning with some flavor of R-devel: ``` r foghorn::cran_details("winch") #> # A tibble: 1 × 7 #> package version result check flavors n_flavors message #> #> 1 winch 0.0.7 WARN whether package can be insta… r-deve… 2 " … ``` Created on 2022-02-22 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1) I pasted the current state of CRAN's check result overview at the end. The "-TK" flavor succeeds, I don't understand why. Checking the headers for the details gives: ``` ~ curl -I https://www.r-project.org/nosvn/R.check/r-devel-windows-x86_64-new-UL/winch-00check.html HTTP/1.1 200 OK Date: Tue, 22 Feb 2022 04:10:04 GMT Server: Apache Last-Modified: Sun, 20 Feb 2022 03:09:28 GMT ETag: "1519-5d86a71a1f6eb" Accept-Ranges: bytes Content-Length: 5401 Vary: Accept-Encoding Content-Type: text/html ~ curl -I https://www.r-project.org/nosvn/R.check/r-devel-windows-x86_64-new-TK/winch-00check.html HTTP/1.1 200 OK Date: Tue, 22 Feb 2022 04:10:15 GMT Server: Apache Last-Modified: Mon, 21 Feb 2022 16:03:34 GMT ETag: "1320-5d8895fe12319" Accept-Ranges: bytes Content-Length: 4896 Vary: Accept-Encoding Content-Type: text/html ``` The `Last-Modified:` entry coincides with the R versions shown in the log: r81760 vs. r81775. title: timestamps on CRAN incoming might not be reliable?
description:
Now that I've added timestamps to `cran_incoming()`, I'm wondering how reliable they are for answering the question I thought they answered (when a package entered a specified folder/category). title: does winbuilder_queue() work?
description:
`winbuilder_queue()` seems to be returning an empty tibble, even while I've got a package that I know is in process there.  Does that mean (1) something is broken/has changed about the setup or (2) only packages that are *waiting*, not packages being processed, are listed?

I think there must be at least part of `#1` above going on, because directly visiting the URL (ftp://win-builder.r-project.org/R-devel/) shows three packages in the queue (including mine) even while `winbuilder_queue()` is returning the empty tibble. 

PS I think some of `#2` must apply as well, as the URL above (and the corresponding R-release one) are now empty, but I haven't received an updated status e-mail yet. (Assuming that the package testing is in progress - another possibility is that there's a surprisingly large lag between the end of the package testing process and my receipt of the status e-mail?)

title: Erroneous Invalid package name due to timeout
description:
### Problem

A timeout from CRAN causes `read_cran_from_web()` to return an "Invalid package name" error.

### Details

I was attempting to release a package using devtools today when I got a weird error stemming from foghorn:

```r
Error: Invalid package name(s): ‘incidence’.
> traceback()
6: stop("Invalid package name(s): ", paste(sQuote(pkg[bad]), collapse = ", "), 
       ".", call. = FALSE)
5: read_cran_web_from_pkg(pkg, ...)
4: cran_results_web(email, pkg, ...)
3: foghorn::cran_results(pkg = pkg, show = c("error", "fail", "warn", 
       "note"))
2: has_cran_results(pkg$package)
1: devtools::release()
```

I was a bit miffed because when I tried the below command it worked once and then gave me the same error.

```r
> foghorn::cran_results(pkg = "incidence", show = c("error", "fail", "warn", "note"))
Error: Invalid package name(s): ‘incidence’.
```

When I tried the traceback from `read_cran_web_from_pkg()`, it (frustratingly) worked. So, I tried to go one level deeper:

```r
> foghorn::cran_results(pkg = "incidence", show = c("error", "fail", "warn", "note"))
Error: Invalid package name(s): ‘incidence’.
> debugonce(foghorn:::read_cran_web)
> foghorn::cran_results(pkg = "incidence", show = c("error", "fail", "warn", "note"))
debugging in: FUN(X[[i]], ...)
debug: {
    if (!curl::has_internet()) {
        stop("No internet connection detected", call. = FALSE)
    }
    .res <- try(xml2::read_html(x), silent = TRUE)
    if (inherits(.res, "try-error")) {
        ss <- showConnections(all = TRUE)
        cc <- as.numeric(rownames(ss)[ss[, 1] == x])
        if (length(cc) > 0) 
            on.exit(close(getConnection(cc)))
        return(NA)
    }
    return(.res)
}
Browse[2]> 
debug: if (!curl::has_internet()) {
    stop("No internet connection detected", call. = FALSE)
}
Browse[2]> 
debug: .res <- try(xml2::read_html(x), silent = TRUE)
Browse[2]> 
debug: if (inherits(.res, "try-error")) {
    ss <- showConnections(all = TRUE)
    cc <- as.numeric(rownames(ss)[ss[, 1] == x])
    if (length(cc) > 0) 
        on.exit(close(getConnection(cc)))
    return(NA)
}
Browse[2]> .res
[1] "Error in open.connection(x, \"rb\") : \n  Timeout was reached: Connection timed out after 10001 milliseconds\n"
attr(,"class")
[1] "try-error"
attr(,"condition")
<simpleError in open.connection(x, "rb"): Timeout was reached: Connection timed out after 10001 milliseconds>
```

It turns out that the error I was getting was because `read_cran_web()` was returning `NA` for an error caused by a timeout as opposed to a malformed package name.

title: Cleaner separation between computation and display?
description: Foghorn would be a bit easier to use programmatically if you factored the functions a little differently. Currently you have `check_cran_results()` and `summary_cran_results()` to retrieve summary tables for one or more packages, and `show_cran_results()` to show the detailed results for a single package. I think the API would be a little more elegant if you had `cran_results()` and `cran_details()` functions. `check_cran_results()` would become `cran_results()`, and `summary_cran_results` would become a summary method; `show_cran_results()` would become a print method for the object returned by `cran_details()`. This would also make foghorn easier to program with since you've separate the two tasks of parsing the results from the webpage and displaying attractive results to the user.

maintainer addresses with non-standard characters
description:
**tl;dr** the maintainer-e-mail-to-URL conversion should also have a `gsub()` step substituting underscores for special characters ...

The [CRAN checks-by-maintainer page](https://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_summary_by_maintainer.html) says:

 > Maintainers can directly adress [sic] their results via https://CRAN.R-project.org/web/checks/check_summary_by_maintainer.html#address:id, where id is obtained from the shown email address with all characters different from letters, digits, hyphens, underscores, colons, and periods replaced by underscores.

(Let's hope there aren't two CRAN maintainers with e-mail addresses disambiguated *only* by special characters ...)

This is a little misleading or incomplete: the form shown above takes you to an *anchor* on the full CRAN form, whereas the form https://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_results_address.html takes you to a maintainer-specific page (also, typo in "adress" above ... I know these are CRAN's problems, not yours ...)

The maintainer address for `lme4` is "bbolker+lme4 at gmail.com".  This means I can get there via https://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_results_bbolker_lme4_at_gmail.com.html ... 

(I got very confused while working on  this issue, I think I was just trying a whole bunch of slightly wrong things.)

title: Suggestions/requests
description:
Hey! I saw [your tweet][0] and I have some feedback. First, thank you for putting this together! It's nice not having to go to different cran check pages just to check the status every time a new version is released :)


## Bugs?

It works well so far, but I ran into some weirdness. It works for my main package, poppr, but it seems to be missing out on ezec:

```r
foghorn::summary_cran_checks(email = "kamvarz@science.oregonstate.edu")
## ✖ Package(s) with errors on CRAN: poppr, popprxl

foghorn::summary_cran_checks(package = c("poppr", "popprxl", "ezec", "adegenet", "mmod"))
##✖ Package(s) with errors on CRAN: adegenet, poppr, popprxl
## Warning message:
## closing unused connection 3 (https://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_results_zkamvar_at_gmail.com.html)
```


## Suggestion

Additionally, it would be nice to have the number of errors in the summary instead of just errors e.g:

```r
## ✖ Package(s) with errors on CRAN: poppr (2/13), popprxl (2/13)
```

This way, it's easier to see whether or not the errors are new.

[0]: https://twitter.com/fmic_/status/793577021150490625
